title: Redcap and airport restroom incidents
summary: In Atlanta a Black redcap refused to put her in her drawing room until a white redcap did. In an airport she walked into the white restroom and told the attendant she would not leave without using it.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well, I'll tell you what Helen, you did tell, I think you told Stanley a story about the South. I don't think you were performing or traveling or anything. You were going down somewhere with . . .

Yeah, I was down in Atlanta, Georgia and I had my reservations and I had a drawing room --the redcap-- when I got to the station and he said, I can't put you on that train. I said, "what you mean you can't put me on there?" "Because that's a drawing room". I said, "yes I bought that. I got it". So he said, "well I can't put you on". And he was colored. The white one came and I said, " I got my ticket here and I got a drawing room on this train". He said, "alright come right on". And he put me right on.
Sometimes people just don't have the guts.

This isn't the colored rest-room". I said, "I aint looking for no colored restrooms. I'm just looking for a restroom". And I said, "I'm in one and I aint going out of here without using it". So she said, "well next time you come you have to go to the colored restroom". I said, "well, there won't be no next time. I'm here now". So that was that. That was the only trouble I had.
